Here's my assessment:

---

## Config Audit — pnpm 9.15.0 vs. Current Upstream (11.25.0 / 12.3.2)

### Files audited

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `package.json:9` | `"packageManager": "pnpm@9.15.0"` |
| `.npmrc:1-10` | `shamefully-hoist=true`, `strict-peer-dependencies=false`, `lockfile=true` |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-3` | `packages: [apps/*, packages/*]` |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml:1-5` | lockfileVersion `9.0`, `autoInstallPeers: true`, `excludeLinksFromLockfile: false` |

### Verdict: **No breakage today; a migration hazard on upgrade.**

On **pnpm 9** the config is read correctly — `.npmrc` is still a general settings source. But the **pnpm 11 docs** now say:

> "Only auth and registry settings are read from `.npmrc` files. All other settings (like `hoistPattern`, `nodeLinker`, `shamefullyHoist`, etc.) must be configured in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml`."
> — https://pnpm.io/settings (accessed 2026-09-05)

If anyone runs this workspace under pnpm 11+, `shamefully-hoist=true` and `strict-peer-dependencies=false` would be **silently ignored**, changing install behavior without warning. The `lockfile=true` is the default and harmless regardless.

### Per-setting detail

| `.npmrc` setting | pnpm 9 behavior | pnpm 11+ risk |
|---|---|---|
| `shamefully-hoist=true` | Works — hoists all deps to root `node_modules` | **Silently ignored** → deps revert to strict isolation; tooling that needs phantom deps will break |
| `strict-peer-dependencies=false` | Works — warnings only, no hard failure | **Silently ignored** → reverts to default (`false`), so same behavior by coincidence — but the explicit intent is lost |
| `lockfile=true` | Works (also the default) | Read by `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `lockfile` setting; `.npmrc` form ignored, but since `true` is the default, no behavior change |

### Recommended minimal change (optional, forward-proofing)

Move the two non-default settings into `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and remove them from `.npmrc`. This makes the config correct on **both** pnpm 9 and 11+ without changing behavior.

**`pnpm-workspace.yaml`** — add:
```yaml
shamefullyHoist: true
strictPeerDependencies: false
```

**`.npmrc`** — remove those two lines; keep `lockfile=true` only if you want the explicit signal (it's the default either way).

No `packageManager` version bump is required — the project stays on 9.15.0 and everything works identically, but is now future-proof.

### Sources checked

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| pnpm settings (12.x, current docs) | https://pnpm.io/settings |
| pnpm settings (10.x, last `.npmrc`-permissive) | https://pnpm.io/10.x/settings |
| pnpm `shamefullyHoist` reference | https://pnpm.io/settings/node-modules#shamefullyhoist |
| pnpm `strictPeerDependencies` reference | https://pnpm.io/settings/peer-dependencies#strictpeerdependencies |
| pnpm `lockfile` reference | https://pnpm.io/settings/store#lockfile |
| pnpm 11.25.0 release (latest 11.x) | https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.25.0 |
| pnpm 12.0 release notes | https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/12.0 |
| npm registry latest version | https://www.npmjs.com/package/pnpm |
